name: After School Special: SVA Alumni Film + Animation Festival
why: SVA alumni screen award-winning films and new works including Anora and KPOP Demon Hunters, with Q&As; runs through Sunday Sept 27.

name: 27th On Sale: FIT Fashion Sale
venue: FIT John E. Reeves Great Hall
why: FIT's inaugural fashion sale offers 2,500+ new and vintage designer pieces at up to 70% off, with preloved items from Jessica Chastain, Laura Dern and Tracee Ellis Ross; also runs Thursday 9/24.

name: 8th Annual Mobile Dance Film Festival
why: Film festival dedicated to dance films created entirely on mobile devices screens 12 new international shorts; also runs Thursday 9/24.

name: Gather Round: Let's Dance – Brooklyn Contra Barn Dance
why: Brooklyn Contra hosts a participatory barn dance featuring live traditional Appalachian and Irish tunes; beginner-friendly with instructions before the dance.

name: Digital Oblivion: How Autocrats Engineer Forgetting
venue: Craig Newmark Graduate School of Journalism at CUNY
why: Roundtable with Masha Gessen (NYT, 2026 Pulitzer winner), Steven Feldstein (Carnegie Endowment), and Sarah Myers West (AI Now Institute) on how censorship and information overload erase history.

name: Fall for Dance Festival
why: Annual festival featuring 11 premieres and seven international companies including the Royal Ballet and Gauthier Dance; runs through October 3.

name: The Nonsense Lab – Target Margin Theater Festival
why: Three-week festival of new works exploring poetry and nonsense through music, dance, puppetry, and toy theater, anchored by three productions and one-time events; runs through October 3.

name: Art + Furniture: Designers, Makers, and Advocates
venue: New York School of Interior Design Gallery
source: New York School of Interior Design
why: Exhibition tracing the art and studio furniture movements of the late 1960s through early 1990s with works by Donald Judd, Wendell Castle, Gaetano Pesce, and 17 other artists; opening reception Sept 24.

name: New Museum Fall Exhibitions (Arthur Jafa, The Bowery, and more)
why: New Museum reopens with four fall exhibitions: Arthur Jafa's most comprehensive survey, The Bowery: Devil's Mile, Diego Marcon's Arrivederci Piggies!, and a site-specific video by Ho Tzu Nyen; runs through Jan 31, 2027.

name: 260 Madison Art Exhibition
why: 50+ artists take over a 23,000 sq ft former Duane Reade and office floor with sculpture, new media, and video exploring surveillance, AI, and labor; opening reception Sept 24, runs through Nov 22.

name: University Open Air: Fall Edition
why: Immigrant academics trained outside the U.S. offer free public classes on topics including bird flight, feminist art, free will, and tea and China's first Opium War; runs through October 4.

name: CJ Hendry's Flower Market
why: Artist CJ Hendry fills Rockefeller Center's plaza with oversized plush blooms inspired by NYC-native flowers; take one home for free, additional pieces are $5; runs through Sunday.

name: Shepard Fairey's Untitled (Art Car)
why: Shepard Fairey transforms a 1937 Packard sedan into a rolling canvas of hip-hop and punk icons; the four-day exhibit includes new prints, original artworks, and talks.

name: 14th Annual MORUS Film Festival
venue: Community Gardens and Tompkins Square Park
why: Museum of Reclaimed Urban Space screens films examining the rapidly evolving surveillance state in community gardens and Tompkins Square Park.

name: Ric Burns and James Sanders – 'New York: The Future of Cities'
venue: Schimmel Center for the Arts at Pace University
why: Filmmakers Ric Burns and James Sanders screen highlights from their new two-part documentary on Lower Manhattan's transformation, followed by a conversation with architect Vishaan Chakrabarti.

name: The Dead Ladies Show NYC: Indira Gandhi, Mary Shelley, Maria Callas
why: Bimonthly show featuring engaging presentations on three trailblazing historical women: Indira Gandhi, Mary Shelley, and Maria Callas.

name: The Klezmatics + Friends: Celebrating 40 Years of Radical Joy
why: One-night-only 40th anniversary celebration for the Klezmatics, featuring music from all 14 recordings, a focus on their Woody Guthrie collaborations, and special guests including Janis Ian and Lavender Light Gospel Choir.

name: Niche Night: Y2K Baby One More Time
why: DJs Cor and Steve Reynolds spin 90s and early 2000s pop, R&B, rock, and dance floor favorites in a free throwback party.

name: Crystal Visions – Stevie Nicks Greatest Hits Drag Show
why: Prideshow at the Sideshow and Sissy Fist present a night of drag artists performing Stevie Nicks hits including 'Silver Springs,' 'Landslide,' and 'Edge of Seventeen.'

name: Dizzy's Club Late Night Sessions
why: Intimate late-night jazz sessions spotlight emerging artists with jam session Fridays, vocal jams, and dance sessions; runs Thursday–Saturday.

name: Newsweek AI Health Summit
why: Summit examining how health system leaders are closing the AI implementation gap, with speakers from Nvidia, Eli Lilly, and Stanford Medicine on drug discovery and personalized treatment.

name: Everesteer Hedge Fund Hackathon: New York City
why: Participants use frontier AI to build quantitative models, submit predictions, and compete in accelerated live rounds with a $1,000 prize pool.

name: Harness Engineering & Model Wrangling Hackathon (MongoDB)
why: Build persistent, adaptive AI agents using MongoDB Atlas, Vector Search, and Agentic Memory in this in-person hackathon.

name: MongoDB.local NYC: For Founders Building What's Next
why: Technical sessions, live demos, workshops, and founder networking around intelligent data; eligible founders attend free with Atlas credits and expert office hours.

name: Forging Ahead: Recent Acquisitions of Black Women Artists
time: Opening reception 6 PM Sept 24; exhibition runs through Mar 27, 2027
venue: Schomburg Center for Research in Black Culture
why: Exhibition of 21 Black women artists working across media—exploring body iconography, futurism, spirituality, and the mapping of Black history—drawn from the Schomburg Center's recent acquisitions; opening reception Sept 24.

name: Annual Dr. Sunil Kothari Lecture: Rama Vaidyanathan on Bharatanatyam
source: NYPL Library for the Performing Arts
why: Indian bharatnatyam artist Rama Vaidyanathan presents a lecture and dance demonstration titled 'The Balanced Breath: Dance of Inner Equilibrium'; also available online.

name: Winnie-the-Pooh at 100: Birthday Celebration
why: Centenary birthday event for Winnie-the-Pooh (first published October 1926), featuring the anniversary display of original mockups and the new Roo toy gifted by Queen Camilla on its first public display.

name: Data & Society: Who Gets to Decide How AI Enters Our Schools?
why: Natasha Singer (author, Coding Kids: Big Tech's Battle to Remake Public Schools) and Meredith Broussard (NYU journalism professor) discuss how AI is entering NYC classrooms and who is shaping those decisions; also online.

name: Choosing the End: Ethics & Medical Aid in Dying
why: Johns Hopkins Berman Institute bioethicists Jeffrey Kahn and Anna Mastroianni present the core issues around whether terminally ill individuals should be allowed to hasten their death, and the ethical challenges it presents; also online.

name: FLOODLINES
why: Evening of music, poetry, science, and conversation about what happens when waters rise and how cities heal—hosted by Hanif Abdurraqib, with music by Hurray for the Riff Raff and Madame Gandhi, poetry by Eileen Myles, and talks by curator Paola Antonelli with scientists, architects, and activists; garden libations and installations.

name: Supper Club with Pierce Abernathy
why: Dinner centered on oceanic ingredients with chef and slow-food advocate Pierce Abernathy, plus an exclusive screening of his short film on alternative seafood and farming solutions across NYC, in partnership with Off The Table.

name: Second Sundays: October 2026
why: Free open day featuring live dwarf cuttlefish by Tessa Montague, community science with Seaweed City, screening of Jean Painlevé's The Love Life of the Octopus, open studios, LaJuné McMillian installation walkthrough, and launch of Marlon James's new novel The Disappearers with Ragga NYC's Neon Christina.

name: Scientific Controversies No. 37: Octopus Umwelt
why: Janna Levin hosts comparative psychologist Dr. Alex Schnell and evolutionary biologist Dr. Caroline Albertin in a conversation about what octopuses can teach us about consciousness, evolution, and the nature of intelligence.

name: Tuomas A. Laitinen: Siphon
why: Multimedia installation exploring octopus intelligence and consciousness through immersive 8K video of camouflage and sleep patterns, blown-glass sculptures arranged by ikebana master Kosen Ohtsubo, and a spatial sound installation; runs through November 22.

name: LaJuné McMillian: Child/ren of the Bloom
why: Interactive multidisciplinary installation exploring the threshold between land and sea—floor-to-ceiling video responds to visitor movement, holographic displays, sculpture, sound, and a virtual oracle drawn from research on phytoplankton and bioluminescence; runs through December 20.

name: Shakespeare and Verdi's Macbeth: Discussion and Performance
venue: The Great Hall at Cooper Union
why: Met Opera director Louisa Proske and Columbia Shakespeare scholar James Shapiro discuss the parallels between the original Macbeth and Verdi's opera, with live performances of opera selections alongside excerpts from the play by cast members.

name: Native Voices Karenna: Lay Our Vibration Down
venue: The Great Hall at Cooper Union
why: New York stage premieres of two short operas—Trials and Tears and Sacajawea: Woman of Many Names—by Grammy-nominated Mohawk cellist-composer Dawn Avery, with Oneida/Ojibwe music director Danielle Olana Jagelski.

name: Climate Week at Governors Island
why: Multiple climate-themed events and activations on Governors Island during Climate Week NYC, running through September 27; ferries depart 10 South Street.

name: Celebrating Jim Henson's 90th Birthday
why: Four-day celebration of Jim Henson's 90th birthday with special presentation of Jim Henson's Harmonious Hoopla, special guest screenings, puppet workshops, a collectible swap meet, and live music in the courtyard; runs Sept 24–27.

name: The Birds (Hitchcock)
why: Alfred Hitchcock's music-free 1963 masterwork of inexplicable dread screening on the big screen; part of the Practical Magic series.

name: MoMI After Dark Tours
why: Lantern tour through the darkened Museum galleries and its horror gems including The Exorcist exhibition, led by a MoMI Educator, with a complimentary drink; runs Oct 17, 24, and 31 (Halloween).

name: Overexposed: Art, Technology, and the Body
why: Exhibition combining research-based films with artworks by 16 American and international artists—including Barbara Hammer, Ana Mendieta, and Lucien Castaing-Taylor—examining the historical and sociopolitical implications of seeing inside the body; runs through January 3.

name: Humanist Modernity: Maciej and Stanisława Nowicki
source: AIA New York / Center for Architecture
why: Exhibition on the work of mid-century Polish-American architects Maciej and Stanisława Nowicki; opens October 1 at the Center for Architecture.

name: Dark Matter U: Justice, Pedagogy, Design
source: AIA New York / Center for Architecture
why: Exhibition exploring intersections of justice, pedagogy, and design; opens October 1 at the Center for Architecture.

name: Why Design?
source: AIA New York / Center for Architecture
why: New exhibition exploring the question of design's purpose and social responsibility; opens October 1 at the Center for Architecture.

name: Art History Happy Hour: Sculpting the Senses
why: Evening talk with curator and a drink, exploring the Iris van Herpen: Sculpting the Senses fashion exhibition; an expert-led in-gallery experience.

name: Museum on Wheels: Atlantic Antic
why: Brooklyn Museum's mobile outreach unit appears at the Atlantic Antic street festival for free art-making and community activities, 12–4 PM.

name: Convening: Blessings for a Balanced World
why: Daylong convening at the Brooklyn Museum exploring Indigenous concepts of balance, blessings, and community stewardship, in connection with the museum's Native American art collections.

name: New Openings Against Old Surfaces: On Gordon Matta-Clark's Walls Paper
why: First exhibition focused specifically on Gordon Matta-Clark's publishing output, centering his 1973 Walls Paper project, with documentary photographs, test prints, original prints, and new collaborative work by Jessica Vaughn; opened September 10.

name: 21st Annual Brooklyn Book Festival – Grand Finale
venue: Brooklyn Borough Hall and surrounding venues
why: NYC's biggest free book festival grand finale: a full day of talks, readings, and an outdoor marketplace with hundreds of writers at Brooklyn Borough Hall; bookend events citywide through Sept 28.

name: GAIA – Luke Jerram's NASA Globe Installation
venue: Cathedral of St. John the Divine
source: Cathedral of St. John the Divine
why: Luke Jerram's touring 23-foot NASA-imagery globe suspended inside the cathedral's nave, accompanied by an original soundscape—a breathtaking floating Earth in a sacred space; through October 9.

name: Clio Art Fair – Fall Edition
why: Independent international art fair showcasing artists from around the world with performances woven into the fair; free admission, Sept 24–27 at 511 W 25th St.

name: 100th Annual Feast of San Gennaro
venue: Mulberry St (Little Italy) + Hester and Grand Sts
why: The centennial (100th!) Feast of San Gennaro takes over Little Italy's Mulberry Street with food, live music, carnival games, and the annual cannoli-eating contest; runs through September 27.

name: 14th Annual LUNGS Harvest Arts Festival
time: 50 events across 30 community gardens; through Sept 27
why: Loisaida's annual community garden arts festival with 50 events spread across 30 gardens in the East Village and Lower East Side; free admission, through September 27.

name: Don't Play with Fire: The Films of Tsui Hark
why: Comprehensive retrospective of Hong Kong master Tsui Hark including the full Once Upon a Time in China trilogy, Peking Opera Blues, A Better Tomorrow III, The Blade, Zu: Warriors from the Magic Mountain, and more; through October 11.

name: Queens Night Market
venue: Flushing Meadows Corona Park (behind NY Hall of Science)
why: NYC's beloved diverse open-air food market with 100+ vendors representing cuisines from around the world; continues Saturdays through October 31, free entry.

name: Architecture, Planning, and International Law: Building Postcarbon Futures
venue: The Architectural League of New York
source: The Architectural League of New York
why: In-person forum bringing together architects, planners, and international legal scholars to explore how the built environment can support legally binding frameworks for a postcarbon future; CEUs available, waitlist open.

name: Beaux Arts Ball 2026
source: The Architectural League of New York
why: The Architectural League's annual Beaux Arts Ball is a celebration of architecture, art, and design; theme and venue to be announced, October 23.

name: OHNY Weekend 2026
time: October 16–18; ticketed access starts Oct 2 at noon
why: Open House New York's annual weekend opens 300+ destinations—skyscrapers, subway tunnels, factories, historic landmarks, private clubs—to the public; free access to most, ticketed destinations released Oct 2 at noon via Eventbrite.

name: What Can You Do to Mitigate Climate Change? (BBG Climate Week Panel)
why: Climate Week NYC panel moderated by photographer Zachary Schulman on neighborhood gardening as a climate solution, featuring community leaders who are greening Brooklyn; ASL provided, with the Block by Block: Brooklyn's Greening Heroes exhibit on view before the talk.

name: We Can't Dream Alone – Madjeen Isaac (BBG Perimeter)
time: Open to public at all times; through late October
venue: Brooklyn Botanic Garden (Washington Ave perimeter fence)
why: Four large-scale reproductions of paintings by Brooklyn-based artist Madjeen Isaac installed along the BBG's Washington Avenue perimeter fence, free and viewable at all hours; presented by the Climate Museum and BBG through late October.

name: Brooklyn Museum Fall Fête
why: After-hours fall celebration at the Brooklyn Museum with performances by Otaku Choir, DJ Jon Ray, Acky Bright, and Shia Ho, plus food and drink specials and late-night gallery access to Art of Manga, Cézanne to Modigliani, and Hopi Kachina Dolls—all opening this week; hosted by Miss Ma'am She.

name: Art of Manga
why: A major exhibition on the art of Japanese manga at the Brooklyn Museum's Great Hall; opens October 3, organized by the Fine Arts Museums of San Francisco and curated by Nicole Coolidge Rousmaniere.

name: Cézanne to Modigliani: Gifts of Modern Art from the Pearlman Collection
venue: Brooklyn Museum (Morris A. and Meyer Schapiro Wing, 4th Floor)
why: Exhibition of major Impressionist and Post-Impressionist works gifted from the Pearlman Collection, spanning Cézanne to Modigliani; opens October 2 at the Brooklyn Museum.

name: Hopi Kachina Dolls: Blessings for a Balanced World
venue: Brooklyn Museum (Elizabeth A. Sackler Center for Feminist Art, 4th Floor)
why: Exhibition of Hopi Kachina dolls from the Brooklyn Museum's collection, curated in partnership with Hopi community members to center Indigenous stewardship and meaning; opens October 2.

name: Día de los Muertos at NYBG
why: The New York Botanical Garden debuts its Día de los Muertos celebration this year, with vibrant marigold blooms, a community ofrenda, playful puppets, crafts, and music; runs October 3–November 2 in the Bronx.

name: Kiku: The Art of the Japanese Chrysanthemum
time: October 31–November 16; Highlight Weekend with taiko drumming
why: NYBG's annual display of Japanese chrysanthemums trained by master growers into extraordinary forms—including the classic ozukuri 'thousand bloom'—with taiko drumming performances on Highlight Weekend; October 31–November 16.

name: 2026 NY Art Book Fair
time: September 24–27; see website for daily hours
why: The 20th NY Art Book Fair at MoMA PS1—the world's premier art book fair—features 300+ exhibitors from 41 countries including independent publishers, galleries, antiquarian booksellers, and zine makers; coincides with Printed Matter's 50th anniversary; packed schedule of book launches, lectures, music performances, and workshops.

name: The Fling at Fort Greene Park – 25th Anniversary
why: The Fort Greene Park Conservancy's landmark fundraiser marks its 25th anniversary with a tribute to 2026 Community Heroes, live jazz from the Brooklyn Music School Jazz Ensemble, and DJ Saint James Joy; bring a picnic or order catered dinner; 21+.

name: Dream Symposium 2026
time: September 25–27; see BPL website for schedule
venue: Brooklyn Public Library – Library for Arts & Culture
why: Three-day symposium exploring dreaming from the perspectives of philosophy, psychology, art, and science—for dreamers, seekers, poets, artists, and inquiring minds; free at BPL's Library for Arts & Culture.

name: Molière in the Park: Don Juan
time: Now through September 27; see website for showtimes
venue: Prospect Park, LeFrak Center at Lakeside
why: Free outdoor production of Molière's Don Juan—a thrilling play of desire, power, and hypocrisy—translated by Stephen Wadsworth, directed by Lucie Tiberghien, with a live cello score by Johnathan Moore; runs through September 27 at Prospect Park's LeFrak Center.

name: Hello Darknuss: Reflections on the Intergalactic Greg Tate
venue: Brooklyn Public Library – Central Library, Dweck Center
why: A special tribute forum for critic, musician, and cultural visionary Greg Tate, with Arthur Jafa, Questlove, dream hampton, and Jelani Cobb gathering to discuss his life and legacy; moderated by Daphne A. Brooks.

name: How Change Happens: Rashad Robinson with Heather McGhee
source: Center for Brooklyn History / Brooklyn Public Library
why: Organizer Rashad Robinson (Color of Change) and author Heather McGhee explore what it takes for movements to win—drawing on more than 20 years of advocacy to argue that visibility alone isn't enough, and that real progress requires building power to change the rules.

name: On Artistic Freedom: A Panel Discussion
venue: Brooklyn Public Library – Central Library, Dweck Center
why: Banned Books Week panel featuring artist and author Christopher Myers, film producer/distributor Karin Chien, and Kokila Books editor Namrata Tripathi in conversation about artistic freedom; moderated by Hyperallergic editor-in-chief Hrag Vartanian.

name: Reimagining Filipino Brooklyn
why: Historian Michael Menor Salgarolo and filmmaker Claro de los Reyes (who screens his narrative short film Sands Street, set on the 1940s Brooklyn waterfront) explore the once-vibrant Filipino waterfront community near the Brooklyn Navy Yard, largely erased by urban renewal.

name: Haunted Brooklyn: Ghosts, Folklore, and the Stories We Tell
why: Halloween-week panel featuring novelist Victor LaValle, Colin Dickey (Ghostland), and Leila Taylor (Darkly) on Brooklyn ghost stories, race and the gothic, and why haunted places persist in collective imagination; led by Boroughs of the Dead founder Andrea Janes.

name: Climate Solutions Showcase at Governors Island
venue: Arts Center at Governors Island, Bldg 110
why: Climate Week NYC showcase featuring live demos from 9 climate tech startups: It's Electric, KlimaKover, Previsico, Rego, Sunphade, Tensora Coastal, True Flood Risk, ThermoShade, and WaveSave—public and free at Governors Island.

name: New Climate Futures at NY Climate Week
why: The largest single event of NY Climate Week at Newlab: connect with founders, investors, policymakers, and industry leaders, plus live demos from 70+ critical tech startups in climate.

name: XR Brooklyn: Worlds By Hand
why: XR Brooklyn event focused on immersive, hand-crafted virtual worlds—showcasing the intersection of XR technology and craft at Brooklyn Navy Yard; free.

name: Brooklyn Tech Expo – FALL4AI Edition
why: Brooklyn Tech Expo's fall edition, themed around AI—an accessible community tech gathering with demos, talks, and networking for founders, developers, and curious New Yorkers.

name: NY Tech Meetup
why: NYC's long-running monthly tech community gathering at Civic Hall, featuring startup demos and networking; free and open to all.

name: Brooklyn Brainery – Fall Workshops
time: Various dates in October; see website
why: Brooklyn Brainery's October calendar is filling up with hands-on workshops including Medieval Embroidered Bug Patches, Sinister Scents & Perfumed Potions, The Cocktails of the Waldorf Astoria, Tarot 101 & 201, Advanced Mending & Weaving, Tapestry Weaving for Beginners, and more at their Prospect Heights studio.

name: New York: The Future of Cities – Screening & Conversation
why: Ric Burns and James Sanders (longtime collaborators on the epic New York documentary) share their new two-part film New York: The Future of Cities, exploring how Lower Manhattan's post-9/11 transformation reshaped the entire city and what it means for the future; screening + conversation at Schimmel Center.

name: Pre-Existing Condition (starring Lupita Nyong'o)
time: Through December 19 (lead rotates: Phillipa Soo, Susannah Flood, Hari Nef, Edie Falco follow)
why: Tony nominee Marin Ireland's raw autobiographical drama about domestic abuse and its aftermath—currently starring Lupita Nyong'o, with Phillipa Soo, Susannah Flood, Hari Nef, and Edie Falco rotating into the lead role sequentially through December 19 at Greenwich House Theater.

name: Vintage Subway Nostalgia Ride to Green-Wood Cemetery
venue: Departs from NY Transit Museum, Downtown Brooklyn
why: Travel aboard a vintage subway train to Green-Wood Cemetery for a picnic and guided tour of the renowned Victorian landscape with famous actors, politicians, and inventors buried there; run by the NY Transit Museum.

name: Subway Swing: A Boogie for the Ages
why: After-hours swing dance party in the Transit Museum's 1936 decommissioned subway station—live jazz, dancing, and vintage outfits in an unforgettable underground venue; includes admission and one drink.

name: NYC Secrets and Lies: Transit Tales (Halloween Special)
why: Spooky-season edition: four stories from transit's mysterious past—three true, one a lie—and only the audience can expose the deception; raffle awards winners tickets to a future walking tour.

name: Transit Walk: Art and Design Secrets of Penn Station and Moynihan Train Hall
time: 11 AM and 2 PM on Oct 24; Dec 16 also available
venue: Penn Station / Moynihan Train Hall, Midtown
why: Expert-led tour revealing hidden architectural remnants of the original Beaux-Arts Penn Station (demolished 1963) and new public artworks extending into Moynihan Train Hall.

name: Transit Walk: Gowanus and Carroll Gardens
why: Walking tour covering Smith-9th Street station (one of the world's highest subway stations), the Carroll Street Bridge (oldest surviving retractile bridge in the US), and the former BRT central power station.

name: MCNY Free Late-Night Wednesdays
venue: Museum of the City of New York, Fifth Ave at 103rd St
source: Museum of the City of New York
via: Museum of the City of New York
why: MCNY extends free late-night Wednesday hours through year-end—explore New York at Its Core, The Occupied City, and Another Wonderland (the Alice mural) for free until 9 PM; pop-up bar with signature cocktails runs 5–9 PM.

name: MAS Walking Tour: Park Slope – The Named Streets
venue: Park Slope, Brooklyn (meeting point on registration)
source: Municipal Art Society of New York
why: Historian Matt Postal leads this new MAS tour exploring the unusual names of Park Slope's streets—Berkeley, Garfield, Polhemus, Livingston—and the history of the neighborhood's 19th-century development.

name: New York in the 1970s: When Music Saved the City
venue: New-York Historical Society, 170 Central Park West
why: Marky Ramone (the Ramones), Lenny Kaye (Patti Smith Group), and Nicky Siano (legendary DJ who launched Studio 54-era disco at The Gallery) reunite to talk about how punk, hip-hop, and disco saved New York in the 1970s—followed by a reception with a once-in-a-lifetime DJ set from Nicky Siano.

name: A Nation in Conversation: David Blight and Khalil Gibran Muhammad
venue: New-York Historical Society, 170 Central Park West
why: Yale historian David Blight and Khalil Gibran Muhammad in conversation on how Americans have faced their Civil War and Reconstruction history—and how those narratives shape current ideas about democracy, citizenship, and identity.

name: New York Hysterical: Stand-Up Comedy at the Historical
venue: New-York Historical Society, 170 Central Park West
why: Evening stand-up comedy with acclaimed NYC comedians, hosted by historian/comedian/tour guide Tom Delgado; free with pay-as-you-wish hours, plus the new 'You Should Be Dancing: New York, 1976 and Beyond' exhibition.

name: Homecoming: For the Harbor (LMCC / NY Climate Exchange)
price: Free (ferry $5 round trip; free before 11am weekends)
source: LMCC / NY Climate Exchange / Governors Island
why: LMCC, The New York Climate Exchange, and Stony Brook University bring together artists, scientists, and community members in a Climate Week NYC event exploring the relationships between New York Harbor and its communities.

name: Climate Trivia & Happy Hour with Green Apple Trivia
why: Climate Week NYC happy hour with competitive trivia on climate science, policy, and action; hosted by Green Apple Trivia on Governors Island.

name: Archtober: Guided Tour of Little Island
time: 10:30 AM and 12:00 PM; no RSVP needed
venue: Little Island, Pier 55 (Hudson River at W 13th St)
why: For Archtober, landscape architect Signe Nielsen and architect of record Fabian Jabro lead a free guided tour of Little Island, telling the story behind how the park grew from a storm-damaged pier into an award-winning public space—including the iconic tulip pots, pathways, and lawns; no RSVP needed.

name: Dîner en Blanc NYC
venue: Secret NYC location (revealed to ticket holders)
why: Thousands of all-white-clad diners take over a surprise iconic NYC location for an evening of music, food, and festivity at the world's most famous pop-up dinner party; BYOC (bring your own chair and tableware).

name: The Unframed City: NYC Harbor Art Boat Tour
time: Sundays Sept 27 – Nov 14; see Classic Harbor Line for times
venue: Classic Harbor Line, departing North Cove Marina, Battery Park City
why: See NYC's harbor art from the water: Jaume Plensa's 80-foot Water's Soul, the Empty Sky 9/11 Memorial, and JR's haunting installation at the abandoned Ellis Island hospital—plus more monuments most New Yorkers have never seen from this angle—aboard a 1920s-inspired yacht with a complimentary drink; runs weekly Sundays through November.

name: Secrets of the East River: NYC's Hidden Infrastructure by Ferry
venue: East River Ferry (meeting point on registration)
why: NY Adventure Club expert-led tour by NYC ferry uncovering the hidden infrastructure, history, and engineering marvels of the East River—bridges, tunnels, power plants, and waterfront reinvention.

name: From Crypt to Roof: After-Hours Tour at the Cathedral of St. John the Divine
venue: Cathedral of St. John the Divine, Amsterdam Ave & 112th St
why: After-hours NY Adventure Club tour ascending from the crypt to the roof of the Cathedral of St. John the Divine—America's largest Gothic cathedral—exploring hidden chapels, stone-cutting workshops, and a rooftop view few New Yorkers have ever seen.

name: The Secret World of Flowers: Behind-the-Scenes NYC Floral District Tour
why: Early-morning behind-the-scenes tour of NYC's wholesale flower district on West 28th Street, learning how millions of flowers move through the city daily; NY Adventure Club.

name: Doll Dressing: Fashion and the Influence of Dolls
time: Thru January 3, 2027 (closed Mondays, Tuesdays, and holidays)
why: Over 170 objects exploring the enduring relationship between dolls and fashion history, featuring fashion dolls alongside full-size garments, accessories, videos, and artworks; free admission, runs through January 2027.

name: Cursed! The Power of Magic in the Ancient World
venue: ISAW – NYU Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, 15 E 84th St
why: 50 works spanning 2000 BCE to 300 CE—stone and bronze sculpture, amulets in semiprecious stones, papyrus scrolls—examining the role of magic from Mesopotamian and Egyptian religious traditions to its forbidden associations in Greece and Rome; free.

name: Forest of Mononoke (Performance + Installation)
why: Saki Sonoda's immersive installation of glowing acrylic sculptures inspired by Japanese mononoke spirits, brought to life by live performances from choreographer/performer Peter Mercury; pay-what-you-wish, Thurs–Sat through October 14.

name: Yuen Woo-Ping: The Number One Martial Arts Director Under the Sky
why: MoMA retrospective of Yuen Woo-Ping spanning five decades—Drunken Master, Wing Chun, The Matrix, Crouching Tiger Hidden Dragon, and more—with conversations featuring Yuen Woo-Ping and Ang Lee on opening weekend; through October 3.
